result_text:
I replaced the two mock-folder rules in `addTestConventions` with one rule in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around line 393):

```java
testFilesConventions.add(new Convention(".*/(__)?mock[^/\\\\]*/.*", "", "Mock resources"));
```

Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as test code, whatever follows it. The name must start at a `/` boundary and ends at the next separator, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` stay out of scope.

Verification:
- I checked the regex against 18 sample paths with `grep -E`. The 12 that should match did, including `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/`, `mock模拟/`, the old `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` folders. The six negatives did not match. A backslash path was not matched directly, but `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` also tries the `/`-normalized form, which does match.
- `mvn -q -o -pl codeanalyzer test -Dtest=SourceFileFilterTest,CodeConfigurationTest` ran with no failure output. No test covers the scoping conventions directly, so the new rule has no committed unit test.
- Nothing is committed.
